bullets.title: US-Iran Hormuz deal triggers broad risk-on rally; broad market opens sharply higher
bullets.body: A US-Iran interim peace deal was confirmed Friday/Sunday, reopening the Strait of Hormuz toll-free for 60 days with nuclear negotiations to follow. SPX futures +1.2-1.3%, NDX +2.2%, WTI crude -5.1% to ~$80.50, 10-year yields down 2-3bps to ~4.45%, and VIX in mid-teens. JPM flipped to Tactically Bullish, raising 2Q GDP forecast to 3.0%; the deal removes the largest near-term tail risk and could allow Fed to focus on core ex-tariff inflation.

bullets.title: Fed holds Wednesday under Warsh; market pricing ~15bps of hikes by year-end
bullets.body: Consensus across MS, JPM, UBS, and 22V is that Warsh removes the easing bias at the June FOMC but does not move rates. Market is pricing ~15bps of hikes through year-end and ~1 full hike by January 2027; Fed's core PCE forecast likely rises from 2.7% to at least 3.2%. Hot May PPI followed a soft CPI print, and 61% of surveyed investors believe financial conditions need to tighten for an inflation glide path. Fed hikes in 30-40% probability scenario starting late 2026/early 2027 if inflation stays elevated.

bullets.title: Cyclicals/value rotation underway; fade QQQ vs SPY/IWM on extreme relative pricing
bullets.body: QQQ outperformed SPY by 12% since Feb lows (98th percentile), with 3-month calls pricing +12.5% upside, 7-year-high skew premium vs SPY. Multiple desks (MS, Citi, JPM options strategy) recommend selling QQQ upside calls and buying IWM or SPY equivalents to play broadening. Consumer Discretionary earnings revisions breadth rose to +12% from -9% in two months; Transports ERB at 40%, strongest in 4 years; Regional Banks benefiting from C&I loan growth in high-single-digits and steep yield curve.

bullets.title: Inflation peaking as energy prices roll; Nancy Lazar sees CPI at ~3.9% in June
bullets.body: WTI down ~25% over five weeks; the 1-year inflation swap fell from 3.54% to 2.75%. If WTI holds ~$85, June headline CPI could fall to 3.9% y/y from 4.2% in May. Core goods CPI declining at 0.1% m/m with a 6-month annualized rate of just 0.4%; AI token prices down 14.6% from recent highs, adding to a tech-led deflation cycle. Real consumer spending expected to reaccelerate from ~2% to ~3% as real incomes improve.

bullets.title: Semis rally hard; WFE path to $200B+ in C27 and $250B+ in C28; AMAT top pick
bullets.body: MU +8%, STX +7.5%, WDC +7.1% premarket on risk-on backdrop and AI demand fundamentals. Jefferies and UBS both see WFE at $200-250B by 2027-28; AMAT cited as best risk/reward in semicap equipment (least expensive of AMAT/KLAC/LRCX triad, potential $50 EPS if WFE hits ~$300B). Semiconductor crowding approaches record 2021 levels; TXN, ADI, STX, AVGO most long-crowded. Taiwan tech May sales tracking 68-69% of Q2 estimates, ahead of expectations.

bullets.title: 800V DC data center power transition drives analog recovery; TXN top pick, ON catalyst watch
bullets.body: Citi estimates the power delivery market growing at >70% CAGR from ~$2B in 2026 to ~$12B by 2028, driven by 800V DC conversion in data centers. TXN is the primary beneficiary (PT raised to $345 from $280) as one of few high-voltage GaN vendors with internal manufacturing capacity quadrupled since Oct'24. ON Semi gets an upside Catalyst Watch ahead of September 16 Analyst Day on renewed SiC momentum. Data center-related analog/mixed-signal sales forecast to grow ~86% YoY from $9B to $17B in 2026.

bullets.title: AI infrastructure capex scarcity remains; transformer lead times 128 weeks, grid backlog 2x US capacity
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley's Sunday Start highlights power transformers at 128-week lead times (vs 12-16 weeks pre-COVID) and a grid interconnection backlog exceeding 2x installed US capacity. Hyperscalers are increasingly acquiring power assets directly (fuel cells, gas turbines, storage) rather than relying on utilities. 14 state legislatures considering data center moratoriums; a 300k electrician shortfall is projected over the next decade. Demand for compute appears relatively price-inelastic.

bullets.title: Hyperscaler leverage doubled to 1.8x in 6 months; $570B+ issuance in 2026
bullets.body: Total hyperscaler IG leverage was 0.9x in Q3'25 and reached 1.8x by Q1'26—rising at >0.3x turns per quarter—now larger than the entire Energy sector and tracking toward the highest leverage of any sector ex-utilities within one year. GOOGL raised $80B via equity, AMZN issued the largest-ever Canadian bond offering; ORCL expects to raise ~$40B in FY27. GS changed its Fed call to no cuts in 2026, citing the capex/debt cycle dynamics.

bullets.title: S&P 500 ROE at record 22%; AI capex near-term headwind to mega-cap tech margins
bullets.body: GS flags that S&P 500 ROE hit a record 22%, with the seven largest tech stocks at a collective 44% ROE (up 900bps in 3 years). However, AI capex, rising depreciation, and equity issuance are near-term headwinds to mega-cap tech EPS. Mag7 underperformed SPX by ~400bps last week (worst week in 3 years); Info Tech net sold at fastest pace in 2 months by hedge funds. GS Prime: HFs net-bought US equities for a 4th straight week driven by short covers.

bullets.title: Anthropic Fable 5/Mythos 5 access cut by US government on national security grounds
bullets.body: The US government ordered Anthropic to block all foreign nationals from accessing its most advanced AI models (Fable 5, Mythos 5), citing national security and jailbreak concerns. Amazon CEO Jassy's talks with Trump administration officials reportedly triggered the crackdown. Multiple desks flag this as a structural shift toward tiered AI model access—US government first, then US persons, then foreign entities—and a potential catalyst for sovereign AI buildouts globally. Anthropic itself noted a 'huge percentage' of its own non-US employees are now barred.

bullets.title: BoJ hiking Tuesday to 1.0%; ECB delivered 25bp hike with more likely; BoE to hold but hawkish risk
bullets.body: JPM and MS consensus: BoJ hikes 25bp Tuesday to 1.0% (next hikes October and two in 2027); ECB delivered its hike with one more likely in September; BoE holds at 3.75% with possible July hike. Fed under Warsh expected to hold and remove easing bias. Divergence in global central bank paths is amplifying cross-asset volatility; 10-year Treasury target revised higher to 4.70% by YE26 across multiple desks.

bullets.title: Fox acquires Roku for $160/share ($22B EV); combined entity becomes 3rd-largest US TV player
bullets.body: Fox agreed to acquire Roku for $96 cash + 0.9693 FOX Class A shares per share ($160 total), valuing the platform at ~$22B EV. FOX expects $400M run-rate cost synergies and FCF accretion by year 2; pro forma net leverage ~2.8x. The deal is expected to close in H1 2027 pending regulatory approvals. FOXA fell ~13% on the announcement while ROKU was up ~1.6% premarket, already reflecting the deal premium.

bullets.title: Accenture downgraded at MS to EW; AI spending crowds out IT services demand
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley downgraded ACN from Overweight to Equal-Weight (PT $177 from $240) as AI capex and direct AI procurement crowds out traditional IT services budgets. Short interest in CTSH surged from 25M to 60M shares in 5 months. Citi notes 50% of investors see risk of negative ACN organic growth in FY27, with FY27 guidance (September) as the next real clearing event. ACN reports June 18 with consensus EPS of $3.72.

bullets.title: HDD cycle structurally strong; WDC PT to $650, STX to $1035 at Morgan Stanley
bullets.body: MS raises WDC FY27/FY28 EPS 30-70% above consensus on 30%+ nearline exabyte growth; bull case valuation of $920 implies potential share doubling in 12 months. STX and WDC could 10x EPS between CY25 and CY28 under bullish pricing scenarios; HDD vendors increasing prices in a controlled manner over 2-3 years. Demand strengthening through CY28 from cloud services and AI inferencing growth.

bullets.title: MLCC supply shortage expected through 2028; Asia-Pacific capex bullish, Korea KOSPI target raised to 10,000
bullets.body: JPM and Samsung Electro-Mechanics forecast a MLCC supply shortage through 2028, worse than the 2017-18 cycle, driven by server compute demand. JPM raises BE Semiconductor PT 29% to €342 ahead of June 18 Investor Day, expecting hybrid bonding guidance upgrades. Citi raises KOSPI target to 10,000 on AI chip demand and fiscal stimulus; memory supply shortages expected to persist and broaden the upcycle.

bullets.title: US tariff rate reset in process; Section 301/232 likely to push effective rate back to 9-10%
bullets.body: After IEEPA tariffs were struck down in February, the observed US tariff rate fell to 6.7%. The Trump administration is pivoting to Section 301 (forced-labor) and Section 232 actions targeting commercial aircraft, drones, and wind turbines to restore rates to 9-10%. Vietnam IP investigation is a key watch item; USMCA six-year review delayed past July 1, likely dragging into 2027. Trump also threatened 100% tariffs on French wine if France does not repeal its 3% digital services tax on US tech.

bullets.title: Oil lower structurally benefits consumer and cruise names; cyclicals vs defensives trade active
bullets.body: MS upgrades cyclicals on Iran deal oil relief: CCL is the most oil-sensitive cruise name (10% oil move = 5% earnings move, unhedged) vs RCL (~1% at 60% hedged). Consumer Discretionary seeing wallet shift from services to goods; goods pricing at 4.5%, outpacing services for the first time since 2022. Risk-on market expected to drive underperformance in defensive hardlines (WMT, COST, ORLY, AZO).

bullets.title: AI momentum unwind assessed: earnings revisions remain anchor; near-term broadening toward value
bullets.body: Jefferies and UBS flag the recent correction as a momentum unwind in crowded AI trades rather than a fundamental break—AI drove ~80% of S&P 500 gains in 1Q26 with 39% EPS CAGR. Earnings revisions remain supportive (limiting downside vs prior cycles), but upcoming fundraising events (OpenAI S-1 filed confidentially, SPCX IPO) and rate risks may keep momentum subdued. Near-term leadership expected to broaden toward value, yield, and lower-volatility exposures.

bullets.title: Index rebalance volatility this week: CRSP starts Tuesday, Russell on June 26
bullets.body: The CRSP index rebalance begins Tuesday June 16 and the Russell rebalance is June 26, creating potential $250B+ flow volatility. Index arb pre-trading may mask underlying mean reversion in momentum names. SPCX (SpaceX) options begin trading June 16, with Russell inclusion June 26 and Nasdaq inclusion expected July 6—near-term catalysts that could amplify flow dynamics.

bullets.title: European data center capacity forecasts raised 15% to >40GW; €1.5tn buildout by 2035
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley lifts European DC capacity forecasts +15% to >40GW driven by secondary markets (Spain, North of France, UK ex-London) and hyperscalers; market expected to grow +21% pa through 2030 vs. +30% in the US. Total estimated build-out costs are €1.5tn by 2035 across real estate, power, cap goods, construction, software, and chips. Five key constraints: Power, Planning, Price, People, and Priority; no large-scale listed European DC stocks available.
